attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his own post. The Fenech quote that follows is not part of this claim.

semantics.note: This is a claim about the state of the evidence in 2022, not a dated forecast. The normalised wording drops 'whatsoever' but keeps 'any time soon'.

contract.note: Reading 'radiologist in an app' as whole-role replacement is fair and ordinary. The result depends on how strict 'no evidence whatsoever' is: does weak evidence of bounded-task autonomy count?

evidence.note: Company disclosure (March 2022) of CE-marked autonomous reporting limited to normal chest X-rays. It shows bounded autonomy, not a path to replacing the whole role.
Retrospective preprint (May 2022) on ruling out normal chest X-rays. A bounded task. It does not address full replacement or timing.
Systematic review published April 2022, but its studies stop at 2019. It supports caution, yet cannot show the state of evidence through October 2022.

reviews.rationale: Nothing in the packet shows a demonstrated path to near-term whole-role replacement. Items e1 and e2 show only bounded autonomy. But the support condition needs a comprehensive assessment of the evidence as of October 2022, and the packet has none: e3 covers only up to 2019. The packet therefore does not settle the claim.

attribution.note: Marcus himself asserts that the claim he attributes to LeCun 'isn't true'. His description of LeCun's tweets is his own assertion, but the tweets themselves were not recovered.

semantics.note: Faithful to the text. It leaves out the side remark that LeCun's tweets contradict his ZDNet interview. 'Pretty much everything' is very loose.

contract.note: Judging demonstrated 2022 capability is a fair plain reading. Since Marcus asserted what LeCun claimed, it is fair to require the original tweets. The scope of 'pretty much everything' is not defined.

evidence.note: June 2022 benchmark: every model, convnets included, is far less data-efficient than humans. That is one limitation, and convnets did well relative to other models.
Meta company post (February 2022) on how far AI broadly falls short. It is not about convnets specifically and not about the October tweets.
2021 preprint, outside the target window, showing convnets succeeding on particular reasoning problems. It does not show broad capability.

reviews.rationale: The packet does not contain the original LeCun tweets, so the claim attributed to him cannot be checked. On the technical side, e1 documents one limitation. The contract warns that a single failure does not establish broad unsolved capability across major tasks. Neither support nor contradiction is established.

attribution.note: Marcus's own rebuttal to a tweet from LeCun, which he quotes.

semantics.note: Captures both the comparison ('way easier') and the stated reason ('don't have to solve the whole job').

contract.note: Comparing how hard it is to build assistance with how hard it is to build full-job replacement is a fair reading. 'Way easier' has no threshold, and the claim's breadth across occupations is unclear.

evidence.note: Randomised study: AI assistance cut chest CT reading time. It shows useful assistance, not relative development difficulty.
ESR survey: most users saw no workload reduction. This concerns workload benefit, not how hard assistance is to build compared with replacement.

reviews.rationale: Neither item compares the capability or engineering requirements of assistance with those of full replacement in the same occupation. That is the measure the contract requires. The packet itself lists this gap, so the claim cannot be settled.

attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his own post.

semantics.note: Part logical caution and part empirical claim that image-task success does not cover the rest of radiology work. Treating it as an observation is acceptable.

contract.note: The plain reading (image successes leave other parts of the workflow unresolved) is ordinary. The contract is also right not to treat it as a denial that AI can process any text.

evidence.note: Contemporary preprint (v2 dated October 13, 2022): report generators from images invent references to non-existent prior reports. This is an unresolved requirement about clinical context.

March 2022 professional summary: AI products are fragmented and serve bounded functions, and visions of replacement have faded. Some text-processing tools exist. It is secondary, so treated as context.

reviews.rationale: Item e1, public before the post, shows that image-based report systems fail on prior clinical context. That matches the support condition: unresolved requirements beyond image tasks. Item e2 describes bounded, fragmented products. Nothing shows scan-reading success amounting to competence across the whole role.
